answer: Anchor every agent identity to a costly, verifiable stake — for example a deposit locked in escrow — so creating thousands of fake agents costs real money. Reputation then accrues slowly, like climbers earning their way toward a summit, and a new identity starts with zero trust no matter how fast it appears. A zephyr of cheap sock-puppets cannot buy history: honest work over time is the only path to influence, so an attacker must pay the full price for each fake voice.
